persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest: Bora Özkent published the first episode of his new '5-minute stock' series today, covering Credo Technology (CRDO), which is also in his own portfolio. He explained that Credo sells copper cables and custom chips that connect GPUs, CPUs and memory in AI data centers, that its customers are large data centers, hyperscalers and Neo Clouds, and that its rivals include Marvell and Astera Labs (also in his portfolio) as well as Broadcom. He noted quarterly revenue jumped from $223.1M to $479M, gross margin is still strong at 64.5% despite slipping 2.9 points year over year, and the company sits on a net cash position of $744M with $764M in cash against just $20M of debt. He said the valuation is no longer cheap, with a trailing P/E of 67 and a forward P/E of 30.8, though the PEG ratio of 0.21 looks attractive. He said his system rates the company 49 out of 100, with fundamentals (quality, growth, debt resilience) very strong but valuation flagged as risky. Technically, he marked $177 as a breakdown level and a daily close above $198.97 as a positive signal, noting the stock closed at $193.87 on September 23; his own system flags an exit at $182.11. He highlighted that 84% of revenue comes from just three customers as a concentration risk, and that ongoing share dilution is another factor to watch.
